entries.real_world_scenario: For example: Can a Darwinian understanding of human nature help people reach their goals in life? That is, does knowing how evolution has shaped our basic moral impulses help us decide which impulses we should consider legitimate? If you do, you're committing what philosophers call "the naturalistic fallacy" - the unwarranted inference of "ought" from "is." I agree: nature isn't a moral authority, and we needn't adopt any "values" that seem implicit in its workings - such as "might makes right."
